headline: Alternative-strategy mix shift fuels a sharp profit surge
summary_short: Revenue rose 30% y/y to $640.7M and diluted EPS more than doubled to $6.95 from $2.80, as record AUM of $942.4B and roughly $13B of quarterly net client cash flows -- including about $29B of alternative-strategy net inflows -- lifted equity-method income across AMG's Affiliate portfolio.
summary_long: Revenue grew 30% y/y and 18% q/q to $640.7M, while net income (controlling interest) more than doubled to $185.9M and diluted EPS rose to $6.95 from $2.80, driven by equity-method income from Affiliates nearly doubling to $124.9M from $65.6M as alternative strategies -- private markets and liquid alternatives -- captured the bulk of record AUM growth. AUM reached $942.4B on ~$13B of net client cash flows, including ~$29B of alternative net inflows. A $14.6M pre-tax gain on the myCIO divestiture also added to income. AMG repurchased $189M of stock in the quarter ($375M year-to-date) and declared a $0.01/share dividend. Long-term debt rose to $3,004M from $2,621M y/y; shareholders' equity fell to $3,038M from $3,239M y/y on buybacks.

drivers.explanation: Management attributes growth to increasing participation in alternative strategies and disciplined capital allocation, citing record AUM of $942B on ~$13B of quarterly net client cash flows including ~$29B of alternative net inflows.
Not broken out separately from the overall AUM/alternative-strategies growth narrative; no line-item revenue driver disclosed.
Company's own Economic EPS (non-GAAP) rose 54% y/y, attributed to the shift toward alternative strategies; diluted share count also fell 14% y/y on buybacks.
Mirrors diluted EPS: net income growth plus a y/y decline in average basic shares outstanding (28.5M to 26.4M) from buybacks.
Equity-method income from Affiliates rose to $124.9M from $65.6M, and a $14.6M affiliate-transaction gain (myCIO divestiture) had no prior-year counterpart.
Same drivers as pretax income (equity-method income growth, myCIO gain); income tax expense roughly doubled but was outpaced by pretax income growth.
Not explained under this label in the release; AMG's own 'Adjusted EBITDA (controlling interest)' rose 44% y/y to $316.0M, attributed to the same alternative-strategies mix shift.
Consistent with $375M of year-to-date share buybacks exceeding retained net income; not explicitly discussed as a driver in the release.
